messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-INC-4123 runtime-cpu-spike on cluster inference-1. Severity: P3. Triggered at 2026-03-14T09:32:01Z. Auto-resolve policy: 5m. Details: CPU > 85% for 1m across 3 hosts. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-INC-4123

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-INC-4123 escalated to schedule: @eng-oncall. PagerDuty incident URL above.

Alex: Acked and taking. looking at the dashboards now.

Sara: I saw this hit my phone — PD shows it auto-resolved at 2026-03-14T09:34:10Z. Did it resolve by itself?

incident-bot: PD-INC-4123 status: resolved (auto-resolve).

Kevin: Graphs show a sharp spike ~09:31:50 -> 09:32:20 on two inference hosts, cpu 80-95%, then back to baseline. Duration ~30s. No obvious 5xx bump in app logs.

Emily: Checked trace sampling and tail latency - no signal. No customer-facing errors in SLO dashboards. Looks like a transient spike.

Alex: Good. Still noisy — this is the 3rd flapping page in 48h for the runtime cpu rule. We should tune before it keeps waking people up. Propose increasing debounce and requiring sustained across hosts.

Sara: Agree. Quick mitigation: silence this incident for 15m while we investigate (/pd silence PD-INC-4123 15m). Doing that now.

incident-bot: @Sara silenced incident PD-INC-4123 for 15m.

Kevin: Alert rule today: "avg(cpu) across cluster > 85% for 1m". That's too sensitive for short spikes. Proposal: avg(cpu,5m) > 80% AND count(hosts where cpu>85) >= 2 for 3m. Also increase auto-resolve to 10m so transient blips don't immediately resolve and re-alert.

Emily: We can't make the window too large or we'll miss real incidents. Add a canary metric: 5xx rate > baseline for 1m should escalate immediately. Keep metric-based CPU for noisier pages.

Alex: Good point. I'll open an ops ticket and PR to adjust the alert and add the 5xx sanity-check. Ticket OPS-728 created. Will author PR against monitoring-configs (PR #1543).

Sara: Also think we should suppress alerts from known synthetic/test IP ranges during maintenance windows. There are repeating spikes that look like CI probes. Add an allowlist filter for agent.user_agent =~ /synthetic-test/ or IP CIDR exclude.

Kevin: Noted. I'll search logs for probe signatures and add examples to the ticket. There's a repeating user_agent "load-checker/1.2" in the trace for the two hosts.

Emily: Handing monitoring follow-up to @Kevin for next 2 hours. I'll update the postmortem template and add the "no customer impact" checkbox for auto-resolves.

Alex: Quick run commands used: \n```
# view recent CPU spikes
kubectl --context prod logs -l app=inference -n runtime --tail 200 | grep -i cpu
# PagerDuty ack (local helper)
pd-ack PD-INC-4123
# silence via API
curl -X POST https://pagerduty.example/api/incidents/PD-INC-4123/silence -d '{"duration":900}' -H 'Authorization: Token ...'
```

Sara: Adding a Grafana snapshot for reference: https://grafana.example/d/abc/cpu-spike-snapshot?from=1767504200000&to=1767504400000

Kevin: Also found three similar auto-resolves at 2026-03-13T02:12, 2026-03-13T18:04, and 2026-03-14T03:07 from the same source IP block. Looks like scheduled external tests. I'll ping infra and the partner team.

platform-eng: Confirmed — there was an external partner running nightly load-checks against our inference endpoint during a test window. They should have used the test domain; we'll follow up.

Emily: Good catch. We'll coordinate with them to stop hitting production or route tests to a staging cluster. Add contact to OPS-728.

Alex: Summary / action items: OPS-728 created, PR #1543 to change alert rule and add 5xx sanity check, add suppression for synthetic probes, update runbook, and verify partner test schedule. Silence applied to this incident. Handoff: Kevin owns follow-ups for 2h, Sara continues monitoring for the next 15m.

Sara: +1. Marking incident as auto-resolved / no customer impact. If it repeats, escalate to SEV2.

Kevin: taking. I'll post follow-up once search + PR are open.

incident-bot: Thread closed by Alex at 2026-03-14T09:47:00Z. Recorded actions: OPS-728 (created), PR #1543 (pending), incident silenced, partner pinged.
